title: Control Flow [match]
description:
## match
When you have many conditions checking the same value, chaining `else if` gets messy. `match` is cleaner - it checks a value against multiple patterns:

```rust
let x: i32 = 3;
match x {
    1 => println!("One"),
    2 => println!("Two"),
    3 => println!("Three"),
    _ => println!("Other"),  // _ catches everything else
}
// prints: Three
```

### How it works:
- `match x` - check the value of x
- Each `=>` arm is a pattern to match against
- The first matching arm runs, then match is done
- `_` is the wildcard - catches anything that didn't match above
- `match` MUST cover every possible value or the compiler errors

You can match multiple values:
```rust
match x {
    1 | 2 => println!("One or two"),
    3..=5 => println!("Three to five"),
    _ => println!("Other"),
}
```

- 0 -> print `Success`
- 1 -> print `File not found`
- 2 -> print `Permission denied`
